propositions: The snapshot janitor's free-space reclaim trigger uses an absolute 2 GiB floor that does not scale to small volumes; on a 30 GiB root this floor is crossed only at 93.3% used, above both the 85% alarm threshold and the 90% peak observed during the incident.

Every review materializes a full ~620 MiB copy of the ticket tree with no reuse because the tickets ref advances every ~26 seconds with minimal deltas, creating ~4.4 GiB/h growth on the container writable layer due to REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR being unset everywhere.

The snapshot janitor runs correctly but evicts nothing at 85% or 90% disk usage because the absolute watermark is not crossed until 93.3%, rendering it structurally unreachable before the alarm fires.
The janitor's promised byte-total backstop is not implemented in _gc_pass and materialize_tickets never calls add_bytes, so the dominant consumer is byte-accounted at zero.

A volume-relative watermark term must be added to the janitor that triggers at a percentage of the volume rather than an absolute floor, with hysteresis to overshoot the trigger and prevent rapid re-firing.

Operators must explicitly set REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT to enable the volume-relative term, defaulting to 0 to preserve existing behavior; the review-bot service sets it to 20 to match the DISK_PRESSURE_PCT=80 threshold from autodeploy.sh.
